chapter: Early 1930s: Bessie Smith, Rex Stewart and the Harlem scene
title: Edgar Sampson, "Stomping at the Savoy" and the Empire Ballroom
summary: Ramirez says the tune was worked out at a Saturday rehearsal, became "Misty Morning," and recalls the Empire Ballroom bands including Chick Webb and Fletcher Henderson.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: What I want to ask you about Rex's band was: Was Edgar Sampson arranging then?
Because later on, he more or less said that he wrote these things like...

No, he didn't write... How it happened. One Saturday afternoon, during rehearsal, there was a number, a seasonal number -- I don't remember the name of it. We were taking the last chorus to play for David(?) (?). And we sat there, and I got on the piano, and he did...[SINGS FIRST FEW BARS OF 'STOMPING AT THE SAVOY']. I said, "I like that." I said, "Yeah, but that's too Latin," you know, because Ricky and Marjorie Gale at that time had that (?), [SINGS...] Yeah, I liked that. So I just couldn't understand it. In his mind, he did. Well, he (?) the chorus side of that. But (?), it wasn't like the one he had... Well, anyway, he liked the sound so much that he took that apart and made it something called "Misty Morning," which was the same thing, you know.
It wasn't really "Stomping At The Savoy" until
he went back...he left the band and went back with Chick Webb. And he left Chick Webb, and went with Rex then.

But anyhow, I remember it, because he came back with Chick Webb's band, and we were playing there. There was a parade of bands there. They had the Paul Whiteman band without Paul Whiteman; it was the Whiteman (?) band, with a singer...Anna Sveum(?). And it had Bob Lowry(?) and George Hayfield(?) -- Hayfield's band.

All these were White bands, yeah. And Chick Webb came down. Then later on Fletcher Henderson with one of his many bands, with Red Allen, came down there too. [INAUDIBLE FEW WORDS], and the name of the place was the Empire Ballroom. Now, anyway, I saw him there in the summers later when Benny...you know, he was with Webb (?) stayed there Benny Goodman picked it up and renamed it, and ...(?)... and all that.
